t.E297.agn: In 1974 JECFA set the ADI at 0–6 mg/kg body weight, updated it in 1989 to a group ADI 'not specified' for fumaric acid and its salts, and maintained this in 1999. JECFA's evaluation reported that fumarates have a laxative effect at high doses; among constipated patients given 5–30 g of sodium fumarate, doses above 15 g caused undesirable side effects, while no adverse findings were seen in adults given 500 mg of fumaric acid a day for one year.
t.E297.body: Fumaric acid occurs naturally in body tissues as part of the Krebs cycle.
t.E297.eff.0.a: At single doses of sodium fumarate above 15 g; no adverse findings were seen with 500 mg of fumaric acid a day for one year
t.E297.eff.0.t: Laxative effect; undesirable digestive effects such as diarrhoea have been reported
t.E297.found.0: Fruit-flavoured, jelly-type and powdered dessert mixes
t.E297.found.2: Instant powdered fruit drinks and flavoured tea mixes
t.E297.prod: Produced by chemical synthesis; it is a molecule that also occurs in nature.
t.E297.regx.1: Not in Group I; authorised with maximum limits in specific categories such as desserts, chewing gum, fillings and powdered drinks.
t.E297.regx.2: Re-evaluation ongoing; a new call for data was published in 2024 (no data were received in response to the 2010 and 2012 calls).
t.E297.summary: An organic acid that also occurs in nature. It gives a sour taste and is used in powdered drinks, jellies and desserts.
t.E297.what: It is an acidity regulator that adds sourness to food; it is used especially in powdered products.
